plain/show.scene: The intern can now refill the machine. Two newcomers arrive during a busy break, just as the intern must finish a task due before the break ends. There is time for a first demonstration or that task. Chief has a full spare flask and offers to cover this break. He calls this a department.

choices.label: Use this break for the intern to teach a newcomer.
choices.note: Another person learns the refill; the intern’s other task misses its deadline.
choices.title: Two teachers. One late task.
choices.rule: The last cup starts the next pot. Show a newcomer once.
choices.result: The intern repeats your demonstration. The newcomer makes the following pot without help. The intern’s other task is late: you gained another trained colleague by spending time that already had a job.
choices.next: Keep the shared skill. Tell the task’s next operator why it will arrive late.
choices.chief: “Knowledge has a second author. The overdue task has requested one too.”

choices.label: Use Chief’s spare flask. Keep the intern on their task.
choices.note: Coffee and the deadline stay on time; the newcomers still need a demonstration.
choices.title: One deadline kept. One lesson waiting.
choices.rule: Use the spare flask for this break; the newcomers’ lesson is still due.
choices.result: Chief serves his spare flask while the intern finishes their task on time. The newcomers get their coffee but still cannot refill alone. The next shift inherits a teaching job, rather than a late task.
choices.next: Name a time and an available teacher before another refill needs cover.
choices.chief: “The emergency flask has saved a deadline. I shall resist giving it a salary.”

plain/point.scene: The notice is still readable and the pot is still cold. The newcomer asks for help again. This time Chief puts down the wording committee’s pencil.

choices.label: Demonstrate the refill now.
choices.note: You stop your task briefly; the newcomer gets the missing first step.
choices.title: The sentence gets a demonstration.
choices.rule: The last cup starts the next pot; ask for a first demonstration.
choices.result: You show the controls and let the newcomer finish the refill. They can now do the next one. The same sentence becomes useful because someone supplied the missing step.
choices.next: Leave room to ask for help beside the instruction.
choices.chief: “The wording was clear. I have reluctantly extended this courtesy to the machine.”

choices.label: Pair the newcomer with an available colleague who knows the machine.
choices.note: Your task can continue; the refill waits briefly for the colleague to finish.
choices.title: Help has an actual name.
choices.rule: The last cup starts the next pot; ask an available colleague for a first demonstration.
choices.result: The colleague finishes their current task, then shows the newcomer how to refill. Coffee arrives later than with an immediate demonstration, but both jobs get done and the handover is no longer a guess.
choices.next: Check that the helper is available before sending the next person to them.
choices.chief: “Delegation has met its natural enemy: checking whether someone is free.”

sign/replace.scene: The cup register is gone. The refill rule works until the person taking the last cup must leave for an urgent appointment. The intern asks whether an exception needs its own register.

choices.label: Ask an available colleague to take this refill.
choices.note: The urgent appointment stays on time; someone explicitly accepts the small task.
choices.title: An exception with a handover.
choices.rule: The last cup refills, or asks someone who agrees to take over.
choices.result: A colleague accepts the refill and the departing person leaves on time. The next pot is made without reviving the old register. The useful rule now has a usable exception.
choices.next: An exception needs an agreed handover, not a new appendix.
choices.chief: “One colleague said yes. The appeals committee has been sent home.”

choices.label: Make the next pot together before the appointment.
choices.note: The appointment starts a little late; the handover is demonstrated immediately.
choices.title: Coffee made. Time spent.
choices.rule: The last cup starts the next pot; allow time for a first refill.
choices.result: You make the pot together. Everyone has coffee and the refill is understood, but the departing person is late. Retiring the register helped; this time the rule still cost more than the available minutes.
choices.next: Use a willing backup when a real deadline makes the usual task impractical.
choices.chief: “The coffee is punctual. We may need to widen our definition of success.”

sign/audit.scene: The audit is complete and the pot is empty. The next break starts now. Chief can either authorize the actual refill or prepare a bound copy of the findings.

choices.label: Let the intern refill while Chief files the audit.
choices.note: Coffee and records can both be finished; they no longer block each other.
choices.title: The record steps out of the doorway.
choices.rule: Refill the pot when it empties. File any useful record afterwards.
choices.result: The intern makes the coffee while Chief files his completed audit. The records remain available, but the cups no longer wait for them. Your first shift exposed exactly what needed separating.
choices.next: Keep only a record that serves a real purpose; keep it off the refill path.
choices.chief: “My paperwork remains intact. Its supervisory powers have been reduced.”

choices.label: Finish filing the records, then refill.
choices.note: The records stay together; this break will start without coffee.
choices.title: An orderly file. A later break.
choices.rule: Complete the register and filing before the refill.
choices.result: Chief files every page and then makes the pot himself. The coffee does eventually arrive, after the break has started. The process is complete and its waiting cost is now visible.
choices.next: Decide whether the record is worth delaying the next person again.
choices.chief: “Everything is in its proper place. Including the people waiting outside it.”

none/assign.scene: The refill rule has worked. The next person takes the last cup but cannot comfortably lift the full pot. Chief reaches for an exemption form, then pauses.

choices.label: Split the refill into two manageable jobs.
choices.note: One person prepares the machine; a willing colleague lifts the pot.
choices.title: One responsibility. Two useful hands.
choices.rule: The last cup arranges the refill; share a step when help is needed.
choices.result: The person prepares the machine and a colleague handles the lifting. Coffee is made without excluding anyone or restoring the policy stack. The responsibility stayed clear while the method changed.
choices.next: Keep the result clear and let people arrange a workable way to do it.
choices.chief: “We adjusted the task instead of the person. I shall file this under obvious, eventually.”

choices.label: Have Chief make one pot at each scheduled break.
choices.note: Nobody has to lift it unexpectedly; coffee may run out between rounds.
choices.title: A predictable round.
choices.rule: Chief makes a fresh pot at each scheduled break.
choices.result: Chief fills the pot at the next break and the lifting problem is resolved. Between rounds, an early empty pot waits for him. You traded a shared immediate duty for a predictable service.
choices.next: Agree who can cover an unscheduled refill when someone needs one.
choices.chief: “I have acquired a timetable and a useful purpose. The timetable is taking it harder.”

none/wait.scene: Everyone waited, so the next shift inherits an empty pot. The intern has five minutes before another task. Chief can ask for one small favor or agree how the next refill will happen.

choices.label: Ask for a volunteer to make this pot.
choices.note: Someone can help now; the next empty pot still needs a decision.
choices.title: A favor fixes today.
choices.rule: Ask someone available to make this pot.
choices.result: The intern volunteers and makes the coffee before returning to their task. This break works because a person agreed to help. The next shift still has no standing refill arrangement.
choices.next: Thank the volunteer, then decide whether a repeatable rule is actually needed.
choices.chief: “A volunteer has appeared. I shall resist promoting them to permanent infrastructure.”

choices.label: Agree who takes the next refill, then make this one.
choices.note: The office spends a minute agreeing; the following task has an owner.
choices.title: Someone has joined the next shift.
choices.rule: Agree the next refill owner before the pot empties.
choices.result: You make this pot while the intern agrees to the next one. The following refill happens without another round of waiting. The arrangement works because both people accepted it.
choices.next: Check the next person is still available when the shift changes.
choices.chief: “Our absent colleague has been replaced by two present ones. Recruitment is going well.”
